chunks: And from him, from Abu Muhammad al-Hajjāl, from 'Alī, from 'Ubayd, from Ya'qūb ibn Shu'ayb, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
The Tashahhud in the Book of 'Alī (peace be upon him) is even (an even number of repetitions).

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدُ: Tashahhud, the testimony of faith recited during prayer
key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of 'Alī (Musahhaf 'Alī), a revered text containing 'Alī's prayers and rulings

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the number of repetitions of Tashahhud in the Book of Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies a specific jurisprudential detail regarding the *Tashahhud* recitation in the *Musahhaf 'Ali*, noting it consists of an even number of repetitions. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of preserving distinct liturgical practices attributed to Imam Ali, distinguishing them from other schools of thought. The emphasis on 'evenness' (shuf') underscores the precision and completeness valued in the ritual structure of prayer.
